case fail_k20_turbo_lean K20 turbo on the stock ECU (MAP sensor saturates, runs lean)
digest fail_k20_turbo_lean hold c13e237c4cb2d28e8800c92cb2fc3bc1efe81a7a93130a63b69847aef5e595a9 samples=39 channels=118
value fail_k20_turbo_lean hold failure0 ENGINE FAILURE — Detonation damage\nComponent: Pistons (K20 OEM cast pistons (10.5:1))\nCause: Sustained detonation (knock) eroded and cracked the pistons\n\nMeasured at failure:\n  Engine speed: 5,500 rpm\n  Knock: 4.3° past the knock limit (peak), 74.2 s of knocking\n  Spark advance: 15.8° BTDC vs knock limit 14.0°\n  Fuel: Premium unleaded (RON 95) (RON 95)\n  Compression ratio: 10.5:1\n  Charge temperature: 70 °C\n  Time under damaging load (part's lifetime): 74.2 s\n\nContributing factors:\n  - Spark timing (15.8°) was beyond what the fuel tolerates under these conditions (14.0°).\n  - RON 95 fuel has limited knock resistance.\n  - High compression (10.5:1) raises end-gas temperature and pressure.\n  - Boost (50 kPa) raises cylinder pressure and end-gas temperature.\n  - Hot intake charge (70 °C).\n  - A lean mixture (λ 1.29) under load is knock-prone.\n  - The ECU's MAP sensor was saturated, so it used timing meant for a much lighter load.\n  - Knock control was at its 10° limit and could not remove more timing.\n\nRecommendations:\n  - Fit an ECU with a MAP sensor that covers the boost level (standalone ECU): until the ECU can see the boost, no timing table can be right.\n  - Remove at least 7° of timing around 5,500 rpm / 151 kPa.\n  - Use higher-octane fuel (RON 98, race fuel or E85 with a matching calibration).\n  - Lower the compression ratio (dished pistons or a thicker gasket) for boost.\n  - Fit an intercooler.\n  - Replace the pistons (and inspect the head gasket and rod bearings).\n\nCollateral damage:\n  - K20 OEM block: cylinder bore scored by piston debris\n

value fail_k20_oil_starvation hold failure0 ENGINE FAILURE — Spun rod bearing\nComponent: Rod bearings (K20 OEM rod bearings)\nCause: Oil starvation: the bearings wore through without an oil film\n\nMeasured at failure:\n  Engine speed: 6,500 rpm\n  Oil pressure: 0.00 bar (bearings need 1.93 bar)\n  Oil temperature: 113 °C (max 113 °C)\n\nContributing factors:\n  - Oil pressure fell as low as 0 % of the requirement and stayed below it for 29.6 s.\n  - Sustained 1.25 g exceeded the oil pan's 0.95 g: oil sloshed away from the pickup.\n  - Bearing clearance had grown with wear (mains 75 % worn), bleeding off even more oil pressure.\n  - High engine speed (6,500 rpm) raises the pressure the bearings need.\n\nRecommendations:\n  - Fit a baffled oil pan.\n  - Replace the bearings and regrind or replace the crankshaft.\n  - A high-volume oil pump raises pressure at every speed; watch the oil pressure gauge and back off when it drops.\n\nCollateral damage:\n  - K20 OEM crankshaft (86 mm): journals scored and overheated (needs regrinding or replacement)\n  - K20 OEM connecting rods: big ends overheated\n
